subject.title: fix(agents): terminate mixed tool-call batches on critical loop veto

question: When a critical tool-loop veto occurs, should the current run discard pending steering and follow-up messages immediately, preserve them for a fresh run, or surface an explicit unprocessed-message outcome?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes accepted session input handling during a safety stop, and source inspection cannot determine whether silent queue loss is the desired product contract.

options.title: Preserve queued input
options.body: Terminate the degenerate run but retain or explicitly transfer pending steering and follow-up messages into a safe fresh-run path.

options.title: Approve immediate discard
options.body: Accept that critical vetoes discard both queues, with explicit terminal UX, documentation, and tests proving the intentional loss boundary.

options.title: Pause both candidate PRs
options.body: Keep both competing implementations open until the runtime owner defines the queue and sibling-harness contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve queued input
recommendation.body: Terminate the degenerate run but retain or explicitly transfer pending steering and follow-up messages into a safe fresh-run path.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal connects this contributor to the current loop-detection and circuit-breaker behavior being changed.
